summary: The document editor's code-block view becomes legion's own (src/mermaid-code-block-view.ts, a new allowed lib.ts edit in packages/proof-editor/AGENTS.md): it draws with renderMermaidMarkup + mermaidSvgElement (INFRA-528's sanitizer) and mounts the SVG in an open shadow root through a new showMermaidSvg in @legion/proof-editor/mermaid, which Dispatch's comment bodies also use. Drawing stays synchronous on the main thread (no worker for documents, decision reported to the architect). The INFRA-528 and INFRA-612 cleanup items ride along. Proof: browser rows R1 (A1), R2/R3 (hostile markup for a comment and a document via a test-only DOMParser wrap), R4 (edit and click) in e2e/mermaid.e2e.ts across chromium, iphone, webkit, firefox, red at the test commit for R1/R3, plus a scratch sanitizer-bypass control.

W (worker for documents) adds a 5 s limit, late first draw, offline latch, caret risk and worker restarts while typing.
findings.answer: Plan takes S and the DOMParser wrap for R2/R3; W is recorded as a decision not taken and reported to the architect.

findings.answer: showMermaidSvg moves into the module for both callers (departure 1); the rules move into the view's sheet and leave lib.css (departure 2).

specDepartures.spec: packages/dispatch/AGENTS.md says 800 nodes is far past what a comment holds.
specDepartures.plan: Corrects the sentence it actually has: a 100-node flowchart draws in about 1.2 s, so only a diagram far past what a comment holds meets the limit.
specDepartures.evidence: packages/dispatch/AGENTS.md:293; mermaid.e2e.ts:196-204 (800 nodes within 32,000 characters); mermaid-diagrams.ts:73-76.

decisionsForArchitect: Documents keep drawing on the page's main thread (as today). Moving them to Dispatch's worker would bound the freeze a large diagram causes but adds a 5 s refusal (200 nodes take about 5 s in WebKit and Firefox), a late first draw after focusBlock/focusMark, no drawing offline or across a redeploy, and worker restarts while typing. Not done in this plan.
